approval.subtitle.proposed: AYAR proposed it from the files of “{name}”. No command runs before you approve it, and approval is asked again if it changes.
approval.subtitle.pending: {count, plural, one {# check changed} other {# checks changed}} since the previous version was approved. A changed command does not run before it is approved.
approval.subtitle.approved: Everything in it is approved. Approval is asked again if a command or a spec changes.
approval.context.title: Context declarations
approval.context.hint: They help AYAR propose what is needed. Every question has “I don’t know”.
approval.env.title: Environment · variables not passed to checks
approval.env.present: Present in the terminal environment, and not passed.
approval.env.warning: If you allow it, its value reaches the project’s commands and is hidden from the log.
approval.footer.summary: {proposed, plural, one {# check proposed} other {# checks proposed}} · {required, plural, =0 {none required} one {# required} other {# required}}, {blocking, plural, =0 {none blocking} one {# blocking} other {# blocking}}
approval.footer.dangerNote: A dangerous command is not part of “Approve all”; it is approved alone with its own button.
approval.export.title: Export the standards profile to the repository
approval.export.intro: This text is written to .ayar/profile.json through the save dialog. It holds no secrets.
approval.export.introExisting: The repository has a standards profile. This is how it differs from what will be written.
